title: rulecad optimisation problem
description: A part to optimise, flat (2D) or solid (3D), in projects/<project>/problems/<name>.json: where material may go, what must stay solid or empty, where it's held and loaded, and what it's made of. Numbers are expressions, as in objects: of its variables and the rule sets it uses. cad optimise runs it; a design reads the result through a variable of type problem.

uses.description: Rule sets: the material's, the printer's, the part's own

variants.description: Named settings of variables with tweak ranges, picked as name:variant

material.description: A rule set with modulus (MPa), poisson and, for safety factors, strength (MPa)

cell.description: The grid's cell size, mm: smaller is finer and slower

volume.description: The share of the space to fill, 0 to 1 (keep regions count towards it): the stiffest layout that fills it. Give this or a stress limit

stress.description: A limit on von Mises stress (MPa), such as "pla.strength / 3": the lightest layout that keeps every cell under it (Senhora et al. 2020). Give this or a volume

filter.description: Filter radius, mm: about the thinnest member (default 1.5 cells)

projection.description: Sharpen the result to solid and empty (default true)

keep.description: Must stay solid: bosses round bolt holes

avoid.description: Must stay empty: holes, clearances (avoid wins over keep)

cases.description: Each load case's weight in the optimisation (default 1); 0 analyses it without optimising for it

smooth.description: Smoothing passes for the outline (2D) or surface (3D), default 4

min_area.description: Holes and islands smaller than this (mm²) are dropped

critical.description: Safety-critical (a pedal, a lever, a bracket that holds people): parts analysed under it are reported unverified until a test or an independent analysis is recorded against them

overhang.description: 3D: printable this way up ('+z', '-y', …), or a variable holding it, or 'none': only material supported from below at 45° or less

at.description: The centre, mm: [x, y] in 2D, [x, y, z] in 3D

r.description: A circle's or ball's radius, or a cylinder's

part.description: 3D: a named part of another design in the project, as it's built: object.part

teardrop.description: 3D: a 45° point on the cylinder that way, so it prints without support: down for a boss (its underside), up for a hole (its roof). up and down follow the problem's overhang (+z when it's free); along the cylinder's axis it has none
